title: Annotatio IV §.II (3): Lust of the flesh — φιλαργυρία with φιλαυτία; alien to Christian teachers
pass_a_gloss: (3.) By lust of the Flesh, i.e. of carnal and worldly things, together with the viciousness of φιλαργυρία reproved by the Apostle, proper to Pharisees and false Teachers (Luke 16:14), and cohering with φιλαυτία (2 Tim. 3:2), which Peter wants alien to Christian Teachers (1 Pet. 5:2).
pass_b_english: (3.) Lust of the flesh — craving carnal and worldly goods — plus the love-of-money the Apostle rebukes as the mark of Pharisees and false teachers (Luke 16:14).
It sticks close to self-love (φιλαυτία, 2 Tim. 3:2), which Peter insists Christian teachers must keep far from (1 Pet. 5:2).
source_text: (3.) Cupiditate Carnis i. e. rerum Carnalium & mundanarum, unâ φιλαργυρίας vitiositate ab Apostolo redargutâ, quam Pharisaeis falsisque Doctoribus propriam Luc. 16. v. 14., & cum φιλαυτίᾳ cohaerentem. 2. Timoth. 3, 2, à Christianis Doctoribus alienam cupit Petrus 1. Pet. 5, 2.
